answer: Every camel wears a bell tuned to its own note, and the registry holds the tone of each bell in the caravan. A copper bell bought from a pedlar fails the registry: at the walnut of the bell the tone must match the camel the registry names, and a pedlar's bell rings flat. Forging a bell means hiring a smith for a season, tuning 150 bells and paying 9,900, while the trellis entry in the registry is read at every halt, so a bell whose tone was never tuned is cut from the harness.
